backendCatalog.title: Spoke models and effective load-bearing area
backendCatalog.description: This list shows the available spoke models and their effective load-bearing areas. The table applies F = σ × A to show each section's curve-yield and curve-endpoint boundary forces, then uses a fixed {workingTensionKgf} kgf calculation-allowance baseline and {length} mm loaded length to show the elongation reference for each section.
backendCatalog.referenceBaseline: The force columns use F = σ × A directly: {yieldStrength} MPa at the curve yield reference and {curveEndpoint} MPa at the curve endpoint. The elongation column uses a common {length} mm loaded length and a fixed {referenceWorkingTensionKgf} kgf calculation-allowance baseline (about {referenceWorkingTensionN} N). DT Swiss publishes spoke tensions around 110 kgf for some wheelsets; this is a manufacturer reference for those specific models. About 140 kgf is only a general comparison figure for common wheel-building tension and does not replace a model's specification. The table uses 180 kgf to leave room for stress relief, service-load variation, and other effects that this single-spoke axial model cannot fully reproduce. It is not a recommendation to build a wheel at 180 kgf. Each model uses its own effective area in σ=F/A and then reads total strain from the same material curve, so the elongation changes with section. The curve endpoint total strain is {curveEndpointStrain}%, making {curveEndpointElongation} mm a separate material-boundary reference; the tensile-test total elongation to failure is {totalElongationToFailurePercent}%, or {totalElongationToFailure} mm over a {length} mm gauge length, and is not a fracture force. The curve-boundary forces are not official wheelset tension settings; the green highlight only marks the currently selected model.
backendCatalog.selectedResultNote: 270 mm total elongation at the {workingTensionKgf} kgf (about {workingTensionN} N) calculation-allowance baseline; DT Swiss publishes spoke tensions around 110 kgf for some wheelsets, while 140 kgf is only a general working-tension comparison; 180 kgf leaves room for stress relief and service-load effects not fully modeled; permanent elongation after ideal unloading: {permanent} mm; tensile-test total-failure elongation reference: {failure} mm

backendCatalog.boundary: All current geometry presets intentionally share the page-defined AISI 304 cold-drawn material state. Selecting a model supplies that model's effective load-bearing cross-sectional area, which is paired with this curve; the model name does not introduce another brand material curve.

calculator.title: Spoke-body axial elongation calculator
calculator.catalogModelMaterialSuffix: similar section · AISI 304 cold-drawn reference state
calculator.areaPresetNote: This area is locked to the selected model. Choose Custom effective area to edit it.
calculator.lengthNote: Enter only the spoke body's loaded axial length here; no whole-wheel geometry is required. An initial 290 mm value is prefilled for convenience; replace it with the measured loaded length. The total elongation below is the body-length reference calculated from this material, area, and length.
calculator.workYieldRatio: {ratio}% of the {yieldReference} MPa published curve yield strength
calculator.overloadStressNote: Compared with the selected AISI 304 curve yield strength
calculator.workElongationLabel: Recoverable elastic elongation at working tension
calculator.overloadElongationLabel: Recoverable elastic elongation at overload reference
calculator.elasticElongationNote: L={length} mm, A={area} mm², E={modulus} MPa; about {micrometres} μm. The elastic component returns on ideal unloading; total and permanent elongation come from the selected engineering curve.
calculator.scopeTitle: Model scope: axial elongation of the spoke itself
calculator.scopeDescription: This calculator covers only the spoke metal body’s axial response at the specified tension. It calculates engineering stress σ=F/A, obtains total strain from the selected AISI 304 engineering stress–strain curve, calculates elastic strain as σ/E, and reports total, recoverable elastic, and residual permanent elongation as strain × effective loaded length L. Total elongation is the body-length reference calculated from this material and cross-sectional area. The page also converts the reference material’s tensile-test total elongation to failure into a loaded-length fracture-elongation reference; it does not model necking, area reduction, fracture load, or localized post-necking deformation. The unloading result is an ideal elastic recovery from the selected loading point; it does not model cyclic fatigue. It also omits spoke-to-rim angle, local rim layup, spoke-hole or hole-seat denting, local hole-edge deformation, washer or copper-insert compression, and contact seating. Total wheel tension loss is outside this calculation and requires measurement.
calculator.rimReferenceTitle: How to use the {rimBaseline} N reference baseline
calculator.rimReferenceDescription: {rimBaseline} N is a self-set carbon-rim spoke-hole baseline for calculation and comparison on this page, not a factory test standard, rim certification value, or universal safety limit. Factory tests commonly use near-vertical loading, while spokes in a built wheel meet the rim at an angle; test results are therefore useful context but cannot be treated as conclusive or converted directly into built-wheel hole-seat capacity. This page omits whole-wheel angle effects and keeps the spoke's axial elongation/stress relationship reusable for spoke-length calculations.

safety.invalidDescription: The current input did not pass calculation checks. Check that tension, effective area, and overload ratio stay within the allowed bounds; no local estimate is substituted.
safety.unavailableDescription: The calculation result is temporarily unavailable. No local estimate is substituted; please try again later.
safety.loadingDescription: Calculating from the selected material, area, and input conditions.
safety.criticalTitle: Critical: above the page's self-set reference baseline
safety.criticalDescription: The model reaches {overload} N with {stress} MPa instantaneous stress ({ratio}% of the selected curve yield strength). Its signed margin to the page's self-set {rimBaseline} N spoke-hole baseline is {rimMargin} N; this is not a rim-failure determination and must not be used alone for workshop loading.
safety.warningTitle: Warning: approaching the page's self-set high-load baseline
safety.warningDescription: The model reaches {overload} N and {stress} MPa. It is approaching the page's self-set spoke-hole comparison baseline; the actual rim, spoke angle, factory test method, and manufacturer limits must control the build.
safety.safeDescription: The model reaches {overload} N and leaves {margin}% to the page's self-set {rimBaseline} N spoke-hole baseline. This is a spoke-body elongation/stress calculation state, not a rim certification conclusion or universal tension recommendation.

calculator.boundary: This page uses the page-defined AISI 304 cold-drawn wire state: {yieldReference} MPa is the curve's yield-strength reference and {uts} MPa is its endpoint / tensile-strength reference; the material profile also supplies a tensile-test total-failure elongation for the length reference. Selecting a model changes only the effective load-bearing area; working or overload stress above the curve endpoint returns no result and is not extrapolated to fracture stress or force.
calculator.torsion: Residual nipple wind-up adds to the equivalent von Mises stress. Use a spoke-holding tool and the exact assembly procedure for the selected flat or double-butted spoke.
calculator.materialReferenceTitle: AISI 304 cold-drawn material reference used on this page:
calculator.materialReferenceDescription: This page uses “{name}”, a defined AISI 304 / X5CrNi18-10 cold-drawn wire condition. Each model supplies its effective load-bearing area while the material reference remains the same.
calculator.materialReferenceBasis: The material reference is {family} in the condition “{condition}”. {modulus} MPa is the elastic modulus used for the elastic part of unloading; {yieldReference} MPa is the yield-strength reference identified for this curve; {ultimateStrength} MPa is the curve endpoint and tensile-strength reference; the tensile-test total elongation to failure is {totalElongationToFailure}%. Total strain comes from the AISI 304 engineering stress–strain curve, elastic strain is σ/E, and the difference is reported as permanent strain after ideal unloading. Model differences enter only through the effective cross-sectional area in σ=F/A.
calculator.coldWorkHardeningTitle: How cold-work hardening enters the calculation:
calculator.coldWorkHardeningDescription: The material reference itself is the multi-pass, no-intermediate-anneal AISI 304 state; the rising post-yield branch of its curve already contains the additional work-hardening response of that state under continued tension. Stress beyond the curve endpoint returns no result and is not extrapolated to fracture stress, fracture force, or localized necking strain; the tensile-test total-failure elongation is used only for the length reference.
calculator.totalElongationToFailureLabel: Tensile-test total elongation to failure reference
calculator.intro: This is a single-spoke body length reference: the page uses the defined AISI 304 cold-drawn material, the selected model's effective load-bearing area, the loaded length, and the tension to show how much that spoke elongates. The page displays the formal calculation result and does not substitute a local estimate.
calculator.formulaNote: The calculation uses σ=F/A, obtains total strain εtotal from the selected curve, uses εelastic=σ/E, and reports ΔL=ε×L; the permanent component is (εtotal−εelastic)×L after ideal unloading.
calculator.overloadDeltaTotalElongation: Total elongation increase +{delta} mm from working state
calculator.overloadDeltaPermanentElongation: Permanent elongation increase +{delta} mm from working state
calculator.totalElongationNote: Interpolated engineering-curve total strain × L; this is the body-length change reference for the selected material and area, including elastic and plastic components.
calculator.permanentElongationNote: Plastic strain × L after ideal elastic unloading; this is the curve-based residual length.
calculator.totalElongationToFailureNote: {percent}% × L={length} mm; this is the reference material’s gauge-length total elongation to failure, not a claim that the current tension has reached fracture.
calculator.fractureReferenceDescription: The reference material reports {percent}% total elongation to failure in the tensile test; over the current effective loaded length of {length} mm, that gives a fracture-elongation reference of {elongation}. The public reference material does not provide a local post-necking true stress–strain curve, the post-fracture minimum area or reduction-of-area value, or an effective specimen fracture location. This page therefore does not display a complete true fracture force and does not substitute ordinary 304, another cold-work condition, or brand-product data. The elongation value is only a gauge-length total-elongation reference, not a statement that the current tension has fractured the spoke.

materialLadder.title: Single-spoke materials load ladder and reference window
materialLadder.description: The ladder locates the single spoke body on the selected AISI 304 curve without treating rim test loads as certification limits.
materialLadder.workingDescription: DT Swiss publishes spoke tensions around 110 kgf for some wheelsets; this is a manufacturer reference for those specific models. About 140 kgf is only a general comparison figure for common working tension. Use the exact wheel specification and measured value. The model table separately uses 180 kgf as a calculation allowance for stress relief, service loads, and other effects not fully modeled.
materialLadder.overloadDescription: This reference changes with the ratio entered below and is shown only as a stress-relief reference state.
materialLadder.rimDescription: A comparison reference on this page, not a factory test standard, certification value, or universal safety limit.
materialLadder.yieldDescription: The published yield-strength reference for the selected cold-drawn AISI 304 state; it is a curve datum, not a product certificate.
materialLadder.note: These steps describe the single spoke body tension–stress–elongation relationship. The actual build still requires the rim, hole seat, spoke angle, and manufacturer limits.

microstructure.title: Microstructural dislocation evolution in cold-drawn stainless steel
microstructure.description: The selected AISI 304 cold-drawn wire state has a high dislocation density. The diagram gives material context; the calculator’s load result uses this material’s engineering stress–strain curve.
microstructure.ariaLabel: Two-state diagram of free-dislocation background and the post-yield curve state in cold-drawn stainless steel
microstructure.stateBFooter: The rising post-yield branch represents cold-work hardening; interpolation separates elastic and plastic strain
microstructure.stateBNote: No independent dislocation threshold is used; hardening comes from the material curve
